translations.text: What does it matter if I give it to someone in front of you with my own hands, or indeed in front of

someone who is not worthy, and snatch it from the hands of others so as not to give it to them? Or if I urge you to drink wine? I do not want us to display our strength among you by performing acts of martyrdom.
Or is this not the work of all the saints? Or is it not suffering and hardship that is written about in the Scriptures?
Is there any rest? Or is there none, again, that does not [?] him until he dies?
But, apart from the rules laid down for us, I want no one among us to grumble or find fault, and I want his good deed to be done not under compulsion but willingly.
Do not delay excessively, lest you do these things while you are agitated.
Do not start before the proper time either.
I have said many times that the midst of old men, old women, children, and those among you who are weaker is not the place for a person to display his strength.
Rather, at a time of unceasing prayer, or extensive meditation, or nights of keeping watch with strength, he reveals himself before the wise.

And whoever wants to practice self-control and endure greater suffering—who in heaven and on earth, among all the people who desire God's glory and the honor of his holy places, does not rejoice with him?
